A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWE-Lancer study and provide readable text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices. The original material can be matched reliably to its retained or expanded counterparts in v4.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of GPT-4o, o1, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, including task success, earnings, ablations, contamination analysis, and qualitative agent trajectories.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds repeated-run API cost measurements, open-source model evaluations, and additional analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, IC and management task procedures, end-to-end grading, user tool, and default agent scaffold remain unchanged. Appendix A.15 explicitly evaluates the added models using the existing scaffold; its expanded explanation does not establish a method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,488 Expensify/Upwork tasks and the same 502-task Diamond subset. The cost analysis reuses the 237 Diamond IC tasks, and the added model evaluations reuse the existing IC and management coverage.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates three proprietary models. v4 adds Deepseek-R1 and Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct on both Diamond and Full IC and management tasks, substantially broadening the evaluated model comparison (Appendix A.15, Table 11).

E3.justification: Section 3.6 and Appendix A.14 add a distinct economic evaluation protocol: measured API expenditure, freelancer fallback after one or five attempts, cost savings, and contribution ratios. v1 measures success and payouts and leaves API-cost comparison to future work. Original benchmark splits, execution budgets, and default settings are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds cost-effectiveness analysis, a brief price-in-prompt ablation reporting no performance difference, and an extensive open-model failure analysis covering localization, premature patches, abandonment, repeated failed strategies, and tool use. These substantially extend the retained compute, user-tool, contamination, and proprietary-model trajectory analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports single rollouts except for pass@k experiments and warns about variance without confidence intervals. v4 averages the new price-analysis metrics over five runs and reports 95% confidence intervals for API costs. This uncertainty reporting is limited to the added cost study; the original accuracy reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Original model scores are retained. New Table 11 reports Diamond IC pass@1 of 3.8% for Deepseek-R1 and 4.6% for Llama 3.3, with 40.4% on Diamond management tasks for both. Section 3.6 adds GPT-4o/o1 freelancer-fallback savings of 8.84%/13.26% with one attempt and 18.6%/33.5% with five attempts. These are additional evaluation results.

T1.justification: The existing pass@k definition is retained. Section 3.6 introduces mathematical definitions of cost savings and model contribution ratio, supplemented by cost ratios in Appendix A.14. This is a limited addition of quantitative definitions, without new proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: real freelance IC and management tasks, monetary payouts, human-verified end-to-end grading, and challenging frontier-model evaluation. The added experiments do not redefine these stated core claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive economic interpretations and qualifications involving historical bounties, API pricing, and verification delays. Appendix A.15 discusses possible underelicitation of open models through scaffold mismatch. Section 4 additionally excludes strong generalization to building software from scratch and narrows the applicability discussion to freelance engineering.

D1.justification: Appendix A.14 explains measuring spending with newly created API keys and identifies the cost-study model configurations. Section 3.6 specifies retry and batch-pricing treatment, while A.15 discloses additional scaffold instructions. Existing hardware, execution limits, prompts, Docker release, and dataset-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and Appendix A.4 expand the benchmark survey with works including MBPP, CodeXGLUE, AlphaCode, CODEGEN/MTPB, and DS-1000. A new paragraph compares reported SWE-Bench scores and discusses task difficulty. The original positioning around commercial full-stack tasks, management, and monetary evaluation remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 inserts Section 3.6 and Appendices A.14–A.15, expands selected related-work and limitations passages, and updates acknowledgements and conference front matter. Most existing prose, prompts, and trajectory descriptions remain verbatim; there is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v4 adds the cost-savings Figure 10 and open-model Table 11 and expands comparison Table 5. Existing figures retain their content, with the final two renumbered. These are localized display additions and pagination changes within the retained visual design.

improvement.justification: v4 turns v1's proposed API-cost comparison into measured, repeated-run evidence and broadens model evaluation with explicit scaffold caveats. These additions improve the paper's empirical usefulness. The gain is limited by idealized verification assumptions and preliminary open-model evaluation; Appendix A.4 also introduces a screenshot-input statement that contradicts the retained text-only setup in A.5.
